# How to Use Project Genie with Street View

> **In short:** Project Genie is an experimental Google Labs prototype from Google DeepMind that generates a world you can move through. With the Street View option, the starting point of that world is based on real Street View imagery of a place in the U.S. It is available to Google AI Ultra subscribers aged 18 and over.

Project Genie is built on a "world model": an AI that creates a scene you can explore in real time, instead of a fixed video. Google added the Street View option in May 2026. You pick a real place, add a style, and describe a character, and Genie builds an imaginative version of that place for you to walk through. This guide takes you through one complete run.

## Before you start

- **A Google AI Ultra subscription.** Google's help page says Project Genie is available to Google AI Ultra subscribers, in the places where Google AI Ultra is offered.
- **You must be 18 or older.**
- **A personal Google Account** to sign in.
- **A computer with a keyboard.** You move around with the keyboard (Step 4).
- **A U.S. location in mind.** Google says location grounding currently works with U.S. places only.
- **About 5 minutes.**

## Step 1: Open Project Genie

Go to [labs.google/fx/projectgenie](https://labs.google/fx/projectgenie) and sign in with your personal Google Account. Click **Create with Project Genie**. If your account doesn't have access, you are sent to the Google Labs page instead. When many people are using it, you may have to wait for your turn.

You'll know it worked when you see the screen where you sketch your world. Google's help page notes that once it's your turn, you have 30 seconds to create your world, so have your place and character idea ready.

## Step 2: Choose a real place and a style

Google's help page lists three ways to sketch a world: describe it in text, pick a real place, or click **Roll the dice** for a surprise. For this guide, use the real-place option: select a location in Maps Street View and pick a style. Google's announcement says the place must be in the U.S. for now, and mentions styles such as "Desert Sands," "Stone Age," "Ocean World," and "B&W film."

💬 Example: Choose [a U.S. landmark you like] and the style "Ocean World."

You'll know it worked when your chosen place and style appear in your sketch.

## Step 3: Describe your character and pick a view

Describe the character you want to play. Google's examples include a favorite animal, a comic book hero, or "a claymation monster." Then choose **First or Third person view**. To change something, use **Add**, **Change**, or **Remove**. When you're happy, click **Next**. Stay on the page: Google says navigation starts automatically.

💬 Example: "A friendly orange cat wearing a tiny backpack."

You'll know it worked when the world starts loading and then appears on the screen.

## Step 4: Explore for 60 seconds

Use the **W, A, S, and D** keys to move, the **Spacebar** to jump or rise, and the **arrow keys** to turn the camera. You have 60 seconds to explore, and a progress bar at the top shows the time left. Google lists known issues for this early prototype: the controls can be slow to respond, the picture can get darker over time, and the world may not look like the real place.

You'll know it worked when your character moves through a scene that starts from the place you chose.

## Step 5: Download your video or try again

When the time is up, you can download a video of your experience. You can also reuse your prompts, generate the world again (it may come out differently), or create a new one.

You'll know it worked when the video file is saved on your computer.

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting an exact copy of the place.** Google DeepMind says its models can't yet recreate real places with perfect accuracy. *The fix:* Treat the result as a playful, imaginative version.
- **Choosing a place outside the U.S.** Location grounding currently supports U.S. places only. *The fix:* Pick a U.S. location, or use the text option to describe any world you like.
- **Leaving the page while it loads.** Navigation starts automatically. *The fix:* Stay on the page after you click **Next**.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** You can see a familiar U.S. place in a fun new style and keep a short video of your visit.
- **For your business or work:** It shows what "world models" can do today, which makes news about this kind of AI easier to follow. Google calls it an experimental prototype, so don't plan real work around it yet.
- **If you're just getting started:** One 60-second run is enough to understand the idea. Try the same place with two different styles to see how much the style changes the world.

## Try it now

If you have access, open Project Genie, choose a U.S. place you know, pick a style, describe a simple character, and explore for 60 seconds. Then download the video and see which details of the real place you recognize.
